summary.text: 车 is the simplified form of 車, a picture of a wheeled vehicle. The modern shape comes from cursive writing of 車.

formation.text: 車 is a whole-graph pictograph: early forms show varying combinations of vehicle features, including wheels, a body or frame, and axle or pole elements. The graph was reduced and regularized over time; 车 is its later cursive-derived simplified form.

components.text: 车 is the modern simplified form of the complete pictograph 車, adapted from its cursive shape. It is not a separate part of the vehicle image.

history.text: Early oracle-bone and bronze forms of 車 varied in which vehicle features they showed. Later forms selected and regularized some features; the curated oracle-bone, Western Zhou bronze, and seal-script examples illustrate distinct presentations of the graph.
The modern 车 derives from cursive 車, attested by the Sui dynasty at the latest, and became a standard character in 1956. This change is separate from the earlier variation and reduction of 車.

uncertainties.text: The curated glyphs are modern redrawings, and descriptions of early forms note variation; individual vehicle features in any one image should therefore be treated cautiously.
Early vehicle uses are identified by inscription references, but the cited evidence does not give calendar dates for those individual inscriptions or a precise earliest date for the graph.

senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 車 for vehicles, and bronze examples include vehicles and war chariots. These attest early vehicle-related use, though not a calendar-dated first occurrence.
An oracle-bone example is identified as a place-name use. Its meaning and historical connection, if any, to the vehicle sense are unresolved.

senses.gloss: wheeled machines; transporting by cart; cartload measure
senses.text: Later dictionaries record these uses, but the evidence does not date their emergence or establish a continuous development from the vehicle sense.
The common modern meaning includes vehicle and car.

limitations.text: The chronology and semantic links among later machinery, transport, and measure senses are unresolved, so no chain of development is proposed.

Some proposals connect the spoken word written 車 with Indo-Iranian words for “wheel” or “chariot.” This would be borrowing of a written sign for a similar-sounding word, not a change in the picture’s meaning. Because the depicted vehicle’s spoken name is not independently established, the proposed sound match remains disputed.
The traditional account that Xi Zhong made the vehicle in the Xia period is not independently confirmed by the cited evidence.

overview.text: 车 is a simplified way to write 車, whose early forms pictured a wheeled vehicle. Its modern shape comes from cursive writing of the traditional character.

components.text: This is the simplified form of the whole vehicle picture, adapted from cursive 車; it is not a separate part of that picture.

relationships.text: 车 is the modern simplified form derived from cursive 車.
